chunks: And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him)

When successive news reached him that the companions of Mu'awiya were occupying the lands, and his two officers in Yemen, namely Ubayd Allah ibn al-Abbas and Sa'id ibn Numayran, came to him after Busr ibn Abi Artaq had overpowered them, he was much disturbed by the slackness of his companions in jihad and their difference with his opinion. He proceeded to the pulpit and said:

key_terms.بُسْرُ بْنُ أَبِي أَرْطَاةَ: Busr ibn Abi Artaq, the Umayyad commander

ai.seo_question: What caused Imam Ali to feel distressed before delivering his sermon regarding the Yemen campaign?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) delivered this sermon amidst the political fragmentation following the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, where the strategic shift from offensive jihad to consolidation led to the 'sluggishness' (tathaqul) of his companions. This event highlights the internal tension between the desire for immediate divine victory and the pragmatic acceptance of peace treaties, a theme central to Shia historiography regarding the decline of his caliphate's military momentum.
